name: Project Jupiter (Stargate New Mexico, Doña Ana County)
summary: Project Jupiter is a four-building AI campus in Doña Ana County, New Mexico, named in September 2025 as one of the new Oracle-linked Stargate sites serving OpenAI. Analysts report STACK Infrastructure and BorderPlex Digital Assets as developers and an 18-year Oracle lease. The campus is off-grid: it was first planned around two gas microgrids, but in April 2026 Oracle and BorderPlex withdrew those air permit applications in favor of up to 2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells, per analyst Cleanview. Analyst Epoch AI projects about 2.2 GW at completion around late 2028. Foundations were under way by early 2026, and in September 2026 more than 700 New Mexico residents were working on site.

Planned Bloom fuel cell microgrid as reported by analyst Cleanview, not a company disclosure. It replaced an earlier design of two gas microgrids totaling about 2,210 MW whose air permit applications were withdrawn.
Reported by analysts Epoch AI and Cleanview, not a company disclosure.
New Mexico residents working on site to build the campus.

milestones.note: Named as one of three new Stargate sites under the OpenAI and Oracle agreement.
Analyst dates, not company disclosures: Cleanview dates the start to September 2025, while Epoch AI places it in Q4 2025 and saw foundation work in February 2026 imagery.
The New Mexico State Land Office denied permits to route a proposed gas supply pipeline across state trust land, as reported by analyst Cleanview.

Oracle and BorderPlex announced a switch from gas turbines to Bloom fuel cells after withdrawing the turbine air permit applications; a new application restarted review. Reported by analyst Cleanview.
Analyst estimate, not a company target: Cleanview judges the first buildings unlikely to come online before mid-2027.
Analyst estimate by Epoch AI, not a company date.

power_sources.description: Single off-grid microgrid of Bloom solid oxide fuel cells of up to 2.45 GW, the plan after April 2026 as reported by analyst Cleanview.

Originally planned as two on-site natural gas microgrids, per analysts Epoch AI and Cleanview; the turbine design was dropped in April 2026, while a proposed gas supply pipeline still faces federal and state challenges.
Developers committed to 500 MW of renewable energy by 2028 and another 500 MW by 2032, per analyst Cleanview.
